notes: Planning proposal for Lumen Health Partners, fiscal 2026. In scope: NetSuite and ClaimsLens; modules AC-UAR, AC-PROV and CM-CHG. The narrative describes five controls relevant to these modules: (1) automated Workday-to-Okta provisioning (narrative L11); (2) Jira request and approval for non-baseline NetSuite roles (narrative L13); (3) the twice-yearly NetSuite access review by the Controller (narrative L17); (4) NetSuite change management (narrative L21); and (5) ClaimsLens change management through GitHub branch protection (narrative L25). Policy statements L5, L7 and L9 are used as client criteria sources. Where they disagree with the narrative, they are recorded as contradictions. Matters for the engagement team: (a) No access review is described for ClaimsLens, for Okta (the provisioning hub), or for Cirrus Ops engineers' access to GitHub and AWS. AC-UAR coverage of ClaimsLens is therefore absent unless other controls are identified. (b) Cirrus Ops provides no SOC report (narrative L25), so ClaimsLens controls performed by Cirrus Ops would need direct testing or another approach. (c) NetSuite went live on 1 October 2025 (narrative L7). The number of semiannual reviews and the change population within fiscal 2026 should be confirmed against the fiscal year dates, which are not stated. (d) Deprovisioning within one hour (narrative L11) is not an attribute of the in-scope modules. It is noted only as context. (e) Several items fall outside the in-scope modules and are not mapped: bank reconciliation (narrative L29), ClaimsLens database snapshots with no restore testing (narrative L29), the incident queue without priorities (narrative L29), and password/MFA requirements (policy L11). (f) No statement here concludes on effectiveness. All contributions describe design coverage as documented, for human review.
